title: IF with a double branch and an integer branch returns doubles only
query: EVALUATE ADDCOLUMNS ( T, "x", IF ( T[n] > 1, T[n] / 2, 0 ) )

source.quote: the formula IF(<condition>, 1.0, 0) returns only decimal values even though value_if_false is of the whole number data type
source.supports: with two numeric branches IF converts to one type that holds both
the division table gives REAL for INTEGER / INTEGER

derivation: T[n] / 2 is a double (integer divided by integer is REAL), 0 is an integer. Both are numeric, so the column is double: n = 1 takes the else branch, 0 as a double; 2 / 2 = 1.0; 3 / 2 = 1.5.
notes: "Decimal" on the IF page is the decimal number type, which is double here, not the fixed decimal (currency) type.
